Q1001.L1t: Landlord-tenant law governs the rights and duties of the parties to a lease of residential property.
Q1001.L2t: A month-to-month tenancy is a periodic tenancy that continues from period to period until one party gives proper notice of termination.
Q1001.L3t: Many jurisdictions bar a landlord from ending a tenancy because the tenant successfully raised a habitability defense, and a notice given right after that defense succeeded is treated as retaliation even if its form is otherwise adequate.
Q1001.L4t: The tenant most likely won because the landlord's termination notice was a retaliatory response to the tenant's successful habitability defense in the earlier suit.
Q1001.L2f: A month-to-month tenancy can be created only by a signed lease that has been recorded with the county.
Q1001.L3f: Under the governing rule, ending any periodic tenancy requires notice of half a year, whatever the rental interval.
Q1001.L4f: The tenant won because the notice gave too little time, since half a year's notice was needed to end this tenancy.

Q1008.L1t: Tort law gives remedies for intentional and negligent interference with a person's emotional well-being.
Q1008.L2t: Intentional infliction of emotional distress requires extreme and outrageous conduct that intentionally or recklessly causes severe emotional distress.
Q1008.L3t: When a defendant commits outrageous conduct knowing a particular bystander is present, his recklessness toward that bystander is established, and the bystander can recover for harm his own vulnerability makes worse.
Q1008.L4t: The barber should recover, because the guard's awareness that the barber was in the shop supplies the intent or recklessness needed as to him.
Q1008.L2f: Intentional infliction of emotional distress is a strict liability tort that requires no showing of fault by the defendant.
Q1008.L3f: A defendant is never liable for distress consequences that a reasonable person could not have anticipated, and an unusual heart reaction falls outside that scope.
Q1008.L4f: The barber should lose, because his heart attack was an unforeseeable result of the prank.

Q938.L1t: CPR combines chest compressions and rescue breaths to keep blood and oxygen moving during cardiac arrest.
Q938.L2t: Effective adult chest compressions need adequate depth and a rate of about 100 to 120 per minute with minimal interruptions.
Q938.L3t: Compressions work by squeezing the heart between the sternum and the spine, so the body must not cushion or absorb the force and must lie level so each push goes straight down.
Q938.L4t: CPR works best when the patient lies level on their back on something rigid.
Q938.L2f: Adult chest compressions in CPR should be only about one centimeter deep.
Q938.L3f: Standard adult CPR requires rotating the body toward its left side so that blood keeps filling the heart during compressions.
Q938.L4f: The best CPR position is with the patient angled onto the left side to keep the heart perfused.
